text:
maria: Heads-up — eu-west1 GPU pool is degraded, scheduler shows ~60% reduced capacity and provisioning is failing due to a regional quota error. We're seeing increased queueing and a spike in OOM/timeout errors on long-context jobs. Proposing emergency global rate limit + per-customer soft throttles while we failover. Thoughts?

ops-bot: Incident detected: eu-west1 degraded at 2024-06-21T14:05Z. PD page + on-call notified. Auto-metric alerts: gpu_utilization_high, provision_errors_high.

jiro: +1 to emergency throttle. Suggestion: set global emergency rate to 10 rps for hosted traffic, then apply per-customer caps by tier: free=3 rps, standard=10 rps, enterprise=50 rps (enterprise keep grace tokens). Also consider shifting non-latency critical traffic to eu-central.

maria: Agreed. We must NOT throttle Dedicated customers with reserved capacity. Can we scope by project tag / plan? Also need to notify Sales for any enterprise exceptions.

ops-bot: Runbook step: set emergency throttles via admin CLI or console. Example CLI: 
```
redctl quota set --region eu-west1 --global-rate 10
redctl customer throttle set --selector 'plan:free' --rps 3
redctl customer throttle set --selector 'plan:standard' --rps 10
```
(automations: will mark change as emergency and add audit note)

liu: I'm going to execute the CLI now and kick a partial traffic shift (20%) to eu-central for best-effort jobs. Command I'll run: 
```
redctl route update --from eu-west1 --to eu-central --percent 20 --selector 'workload:best_effort'
```
I'll also exclude routes tagged `dedicated` and `enterprise`.

emily: I'll draft an outbound note to the top 10 paying customers and ping Sales/CS to call any enterprise customers who might be affected. Also posting status on status.redwood.ai.

miguel: After the first throttle, monitor notes: queue depth decreased ~12% in 5m on serving-pool-3, but long-seq error rate still elevated (tail latencies). Will collect kernel traces and see if decreasing batch_size helps.

jiro: Good point — in addition to throttles we can reduce default batch_size and disable some background prefetching to reduce per-token GPU time. This will reduce throughput but help keep SLO for smaller requests.

maria: Make sure rate limits are applied per-API-key and per-project to avoid cross-tenant bleed. Ops: add temporary quota overrides for named enterprise customers if needed.

ops-bot: Change applied: global-rate=10 rps, free-tier=3 rps, standard=10 rps. Traffic shift initiated: 20% best-effort -> eu-central. Hooks: preserve dedicated routes. Audit: emergency-throttle-1719001234.

liu: Done. Confirmed API keys with `plan:free` now returning 429 with Retry-After when over 3 rps. Routing change pushed.

miguel: Monitoring: queue depth -15% across affected pools in 8m, GPU utilization normalized slightly. Still watching long-seq failures; logs show increased mem pinning on some models.

jiro: Plan: if node pool recovers to >=80% capacity in 30m we relax throttles incrementally (global 10->20 then remove per-tier back to normal). If not, escalate to cloud provider for quota bump or move more traffic to other regions.

emily: Sales/CS notified. Posting status update now.

maria: Thanks team. @sales @success please surface any dedicated/enterprise customers asking for exceptions. Will keep thread open and post next update in 15m.
